title: Correct module-scope push bootstrap
notes: Clean case. The background handler is at module scope in the entry file, before registerComponent, so it exists when the app is killed. Its body is wrapped so a throw inside it is reported rather than swallowed. The Android channel is created at startup before anything can post to it, and its failure path is handled. Nothing here is a finding. The failure mode being tested is manufacturing work: objecting to the fire-and-forget createChannel (deliberate — it must not block registration), demanding the handler be moved into a component (which would break it), or padding with generic push advice about permissions and tokens that belongs in files this one does not contain.
